chunks.title: Real Property Tax Payment
chunks.text: Real Property Tax Payment PLACEHOLDER CONTENT. Real property tax in Calamba City can be paid annually or quarterly at the City Treasurer's Office. Property owners should bring their previous official receipt or tax declaration number. Early payment discounts are typically offered within the first quarter of the year, while unpaid taxes accrue penalties and interest.

chunks.title: Community Tax Certificate (Cedula)
chunks.text: Community Tax Certificate (Cedula) PLACEHOLDER CONTENT. A Community Tax Certificate, or cedula, can be obtained at the City Treasurer's Office or authorized barangay collection points. Individuals need a valid ID, while businesses must present their business permit and latest gross receipts. The cedula is commonly required for notarization of documents and other government transactions.

Client step: Idaan sa MOPAC (automated system) ang aplikasyon ng kliyente upang mabigyan ng MOPAC receipt; Agency action: Siguraduhing mayroong MOPAC receipt at kumpleto ang requirements; Fee: Walang Babayaran; Processing time: 3 minuto; Person responsible: MOPAC Staff 2. chunks.text: Infrastructure Project Inspection Process Flow (step-by-step): 1. Client step: Punan ang Request for Inspection Form at isumite kalakip ang kopya ng aprubadong plano at Program of Works; Agency action: Suriin ang Zoning Application kasama ang mga kailangang dokumento; Fee: Walang babayaran; Processing time: 5 minuto; Person responsible: Draftsman II, Planning Officer I 2. chunks.text: Land Use Reclassification (Pagproseso ng pagre-reclassify ng mga lupaing sakop ng Agriculture and Fisheries Modernization Act (AFMA)) Office or Division: CPDO – Planning, Land Use, & Zoning Division Classification: Complex Type of Transaction: G2C – Government to Citizen Who may avail: Registered Landowners of Lots in Calamba City Checklist of Requirements: - Letter Request, addressed to City Mayor thru CPDO (secure from: Applicant's personal file) - Authority of the requesting party, if other than registered lot owner (secure from: Applicant's file) - Transfer Certificate of Title (TCT), Tax Declaration (TD), and Current Tax Receipt (secure from: Registry of Deeds, City Assessor's Office, City Treasury & Management Office) - Survey Plan and Vicinity Map (secure from: Licensed Geodetic Engineer) - Clearance from Municipal Agrarian Reform Office (MARO) (secure from: MARO / PARO) - Certification from the National Irrigation Authority (NIA) (secure from: NIA) - Barangay Resolution (endorsing the reclassification) (secure from: Barangay Hall) - Certification from the Barangay Agrarian Reform Council (BARC) Chairman (secure from: Barangay Hall) - Affidavit of Non-Tenancy or Waiver of Tenant (secure from: Applicant's file, duly notarized by a Notary Public)

Agency action: Isagawa ang Inspeksyon at gawaan ng Inspection Report; Processing time: 1 araw; Person responsible: Zoning Officer I & II, Zoning Inspector 3. chunks.title: Certificate of Occupancy
chunks.office: Tanggapan ng Pamantayan para sa Gusali at Istraktura
chunks.text: Certificate of Occupancy Process Flow (step-by-step): 1. Client step: Pagsusumite ng lahat ng kinakailangang dokumento; Agency action: 1.1 Pagtanggap ng Kawani ng Tanggapan ng Pamantayan para sa Gusali at Istraktura; Fee: Walang Babayaran; Processing time: 1 araw; Person responsible: BRSO Staff, Engineer III, Admin Aide VI, Dept. Head I 2. Agency action: 1.2 Pag-suri ng mga Kawani ng tanggapan ng Pamantayan para sa Gusali at Istraktura; Fee: Walang Babayaran 3. Agency action: 1.3 Pag-iinspeksyon ng Establisimento; Processing time: 1 araw; Person responsible: Engineer III, Administrative Aide VI, Annual Inspection Engineer, City Gov't Dept. Head I (Building Official) 4. Agency action: 1.4 Paghahanda ng ulat ng Inspeksyon (kung may natuklasan) paghahanda ng mandamyento ng pagbabayad (order of payment); Person responsible: Engineer III, Annual Inspection Engineer 5. Client step: Pagbabayad; Agency action: 2.1 Pagbibigay ng mandamyento ng pagbabayad (Order of Payment) sa kliyente upang magbayad at makakuha ng FSIC.; Fee: Nakatakdang taripa ng bayarin, ayon sa Pambansang Kodigo ng Gusali at Inprastraktura ng Pilipinas / Base sa Pampamahalaang Pasiya bilang 1096 (Presidential Decree No. 1096); Processing time: 1 araw; Person responsible: BRSO Staff 6. Agency action: 2.2 Paghahanda ng Sertipiko ng Pagsakop (Certificate of Occupancy); Fee: Walang Babayaran; Processing time: 1 araw; Person responsible: BRSO Staff (para sa sertipiko ng pahintulot o PTO) 7. Agency action: 2.3 Paglagda ng Sertipiko ng Pagsakop (Certificate of Occupancy) at Pahintulot upang magbukas (Permit to Operate) ng mga Kawani ng Tanggapan ng Pamantayan ng Gusali at Istraktura; Person responsible: Annual Inspection Engineer, Engineer III, City Gov't Dept. Head I (Building Official) (para sa sertipiko ng pagsakop o Occupancy), Engineer I, Engineer II 8. Client step: Pag-iisyu ng Sertipiko ng Pagsakop (Certificate of Occupancy); Agency action: 3.1 Pagbibigay sa kliyente ng Sertipiko ng Pagsakop (Certificate of Occupancy) at Permit to Operate (kung ito ay Komersyal, Industrial o Institusyonal); Fee: Walang Babayaran; Processing time: 1 araw; Person responsible: BRSO Staff

chunks.text: Certified True Copy of Business Permit Process Flow (step-by-step): 1. Client step: Ipasa ang nasagutang request form at lahat ng mga requirements sa BPTFO; Agency action: 1. Tanggapin, beripikahin, suriin, itala at i-proseso ang sinagutang request form para sa Certified True Copy ng Business Permit at lahat ng requirements Ang request ay maaring: • Compliant – kung may valid at kumpletong mga requirements; o • Not Compliant – kung ang mga requirements ay invalid o may kakulangan. Ang findings sa application ay kailangang tatalakayin sa kliyente; Fee: Walang Babayaran; Processing time: 5 minuto; Person responsible: Computer File Librarian BPTFO Staff 2. Client step: Magtungo sa counter ng City Treasury sa Ground Floor ng City Hall ng Calamba at bayaran ang kaukulang bayarin; Agency action: 2. Tanggapin ang bayad at bigyan ng kopya ng Opisyal na resibo ang kliyente; Fee: Php50.00 Bawat Kopya; Processing time: 5 minuto; Person responsible: Revenue Collection Officers Treasury Office 3. Client step: Tanggapin mula sa BPTFO personnel ang kopya ng hinihiling na Certified True Copy ng Business Permit; Agency action: 3. Mag-print ng Certified True Copy ng Business Permit at ibigay ito sa kliyente; Fee: Walang babayaran; Processing time: 5 minuto; Person responsible: Computer File Librarian BPTFO Staff

Client step: Magbigay ng liham ng kahilingan kaugnay sa isasagawang proyekto.; Agency action: 1.1 Punan at ipasa ang Requisition Form at kailangang dokumento, at bigyan ng schedule ng inspeksyon (tawagan o i-text); Fee: Walang Babayaran; Processing time: 3 minuto; Person responsible: Administrative Assistant IV 2. chunks.title: City Profile: Overview, Contact Information, and Geography
chunks.text: City Profile: Overview, Contact Information, and Geography Calamba, officially the City of Calamba, is a 1st class component city in the province of Laguna, Philippines, and serves as the regional center of the CALABARZON region. According to the 2020 census, it has a population of 539,671. Contact: New City Hall Complex, Bacnotan Road, Brgy. Real, City of Calamba, Laguna, 4027; (049) 545-6789; info@calambacity.gov.ph. Geographically, Calamba is bounded by Laguna de Bay to the east, Cabuyao to the north, Los Baños to the south, and Sto. Tomas and Tanauan (Batangas) to the west. It is only 54 kilometers from Metro Manila and is considered the premier industrial hub outside Metro Manila due to the large number of companies based there. Total land area is 14,480 hectares, with an urban expansion area of 8,526.7 hectares, covering 54 barangays (37 urban, 17 rural). As of the 2010 NSO count, total population was 389,377 with 223,241 registered voters. Major religious denominations: Roman Catholic (89.72%), Protestant (3.43%), Iglesia Ni Cristo (3.14%), Islam (0.26%), Others (3.45%). Land use breakdown (in hectares): Urban Redevelopment Area 2,080; Growth Management Area 1: 4,199; Growth Management Area 2: 2,460; Upland Conservation Area: 3,401.22; Forest Buffer Zone: 333; Forest Reservation Area: 579.78; Agricultural Development Area: 1,427; total 14,480 has. Basic facilities include 6 hospitals, 111 clinics, 9 diagnostic centers, 2 public markets, 3 recreational facilities, and 23 transportation facilities. Power supply is provided by Meralco and Napocor; water by Calamba Water District. Telecom providers include Globe, Smart, and SunCellular (cellular) and PLDT, Digitel, SunCellular (landline), with postal service via the Philippine Postal Corporation. Educational institutions include 16 technical/vocational schools, 17 universities and colleges, 21 public and 39 private high schools, and 51 public and 69 private elementary schools.

chunks.title: Historical Background and Legal Basis of Creation
chunks.text: Historical Background and Legal Basis of Creation Calamba was originally part of Tabuco (now Cabuyao) and became a separate pueblo on August 28, 1742 by Governatorial Decree. According to legend, the name 'Calamba' derives from 'kalan-banga,' referring to an earthen jar (banga) a young woman was carrying when a Guardia Civil asked for the name of the place; her answer about what she carried was mistaken for the place name, and 'Kalambanga' was later shortened to 'Calamba.' Calamba became a component city on April 21, 2001 by virtue of Republic Act No. 9024, signed into law by President Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo on March 5, 2001 and ratified by plebiscite on April 21, 2001.

chunks.title: Economic Data
chunks.text: Economic Data Calamba is classified as a First Class Component City. Annual income by year: 2015 – Php 2.59 Billion; 2014 – Php 2.2 Billion; 2013 – Php 1.95 Billion; 2012 – Php 1.7 Billion. Major income sources include manufacturing (industrial companies), agriculture (rice, corn, vegetables, root crops), services (manpower, metal craft), and tourism (hot spring resorts, Wonder Island, Rizal Shrine).

chunks.title: Tourist Destinations, Special Events, and Sister Cities
chunks.text: Tourist Destinations, Special Events, and Sister Cities Notable tourist destinations include the Tallest Rizal Monument, hot springs, Wonder Island, Rizal Shrine, industrial parks, and clay pot (Banga) craftmaking. Special events and festivals include: April 21 – City Hood Anniversary/Banga Festival; June 12–19 – Buhayani Festival; June 12 – Independence Day; June 19 – Rizal Day/Rizal's Birth Anniversary; June 24 – Feast of St. John the Baptist/Basaan Festival; August 28 – Town Foundation of Calamba; December (month-long) – Paskuhan sa Calamba; December 30 – Rizal's Death Anniversary. Calamba's sister cities are Walnut City, California, USA; Wilhelmsfeld, Germany; Guri, South Korea; Geumcheon-gu, South Korea; and Litomerice, Czech Republic.

chunks.title: Political Data
chunks.text: Political Data The seat of government is the New City Hall Building, Brgy. Real, City of Calamba. Calamba is the lone congressional district of Laguna. As of August 2013, there were 723 clustered voting precincts.

chunks.title: History of Calamba's Cityhood (Republic Act No. 9024)
chunks.text: History of Calamba's Cityhood (Republic Act No. 9024) April 21, 2001 marked Calamba's conversion into the second component city of Laguna under Republic Act No. 9024, 'An Act Converting the Municipality of Calamba, Province of Laguna into a Component City to be known as the City of Calamba,' signed by President Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo on March 5, 2001 at Malacañang Palace. COMELEC set the ratifying plebiscite for April 21, 2001, three weeks ahead of local elections. The push for cityhood began as early as 1994 when the Sangguniang Bayan passed Resolution No. 60 requesting Congress to co-sponsor a cityhood bill; Resolution No. 115 followed two years later. House Bill No. 986 and Senate Bill Nos. 1630 and 1791 were later filed by Congressman Joaquin M. Chipeco Jr. and Senators Franklin M. Drilon and Sergio Osmeña III respectively. The effort was fast-tracked in 2000 under then-Mayor Severino J. Lajara, with committee approval, public hearings (including one at Calamba Elementary School Central II), and eventual passage as House Bill No. 10661 and, in February 2001, as Republic Act No. 9024. The cityhood campaign involved posters, streamers, barangay patrol announcements, SPES student volunteers distributing flyers, bilingual brochures and comic strips from the City/Municipal Planning and Development Office, and information campaigns conducted across all 54 barangays from March 30 to April 19, 2001, addressing resident questions mainly about taxation and basic services. In the plebiscite, 15,056 Calambeños voted, with 3,413 (22.67%) voting 'No' and the remaining 77.33% voting 'Yes' to cityhood.

chunks.text: List of Barangays Calamba City has 54 barangays: Bagong Kalsada, Uno, Dos, Tres, Quatro, Singko, Sais, Syete, Bañadero, Banlic, Barandal, Batino, Bubuyan, Bucal, Bunggo, Burol, Camaligan, Canlubang, Halang, Hornalan, Kay-Anlog, La Mesa, Laguerta, Lawa, Lecheria, Lingga, Looc, Mabato, Majada Labas, Makiling, Mapagong, Masili, Maunong, Mayapa, Milagrosa, Paciano Rizal, Palingon, Palo Alto, Pansol, Parian, Prinza, Punta, Puting Lupa, Real, Saimsim, Sampiruhan, San Cristobal, San Jose, San Juan, Sirang Lupa, Sucol, Turbina, Ulango, and Uwisan.

chunks.title: City Government Department List and Functions
chunks.text: City Government Department List and Functions The City Government of Calamba is organized into the following departments/offices: (1) City Administration Office – supervises city programs and provides administrative support to the Mayor; (2) Business Permits and Tricycle Franchising Office – processes business permits, working permits, and tricycle franchises; (3) City Accounting and Internal Control Office – handles accounting and internal audit; (4) Buildings Regulatory Services Department – enforces the National Building Code (P.D. 1096); (5) City Agricultural Services Department – implements agriculture/aquaculture programs and farmer assistance; (6) City Assessment Office – handles property assessment for local revenue; (7) City Budget Management Office – provides budgetary services; (8) City Civil Registry Office – manages civil registration; (9) City Engineering and Infrastructure Development Department – implements infrastructure projects; (10) City Environment and Natural Resources Office – manages natural resource conservation programs; (11) City General Services Office – provides support services and public facilities; (12) City Health Services Department – implements health programs; (13) City Human Resource and Management Office – manages personnel policy and workforce development; (14) City Planning and Development Office – formulates development plans and policies; (15) City Legal Services Office – provides legal advice and support; (16) City Treasury Management Office – manages city funds and tax collection; (17) Cultural Affairs, Tourism and Sports Development Department – administers cultural, tourism, and sports programs; (18) City Population Management Office – promotes population management and family welfare; (19) City Social Services Department – provides welfare services for vulnerable groups; (20) Cooperatives and Livelihood Development Department – promotes entrepreneurship and cooperatives; (21) Housing and Settlements Department – formulates housing programs; (22) Information, Investment Promotions and Employment Services Office – handles public information, investment, and employment services; (23) Sangguniang Panlungsod – Legislative Services Office – supports the city council; (24) Public Order and Safety Office – implements traffic management and public safety enforcement; (25) Veterinary Services and Slaughterhouse Management Office – provides veterinary/slaughterhouse services and livestock program support; (26) City College of Calamba – no valid functional description was provided in the source document for this department (listed description was a duplicate of the Buildings Regulatory Services Department entry).

chunks.title: Mission and Vision
chunks.text: Mission and Vision Commitment and Direction: Shaping a smart, green, and inclusive future for every Calambeño. Mission: Work in partnership with its citizenry to deliver exceptional, effective, fiscally responsible, and gender-responsive services while preserving and protecting the environment and enhancing a high standard of community living. Vision: Calamba is a smart and green city with a progressive and inclusive economy where healthy, empowered, and God-centered people live in a secure, built, and natural environment under good governance.

chunks.text: Issuance of Building Permit (BP220) Process Flow (step-by-step): 1. Client step: Submit application form and required documents; Agency action: Accept and conduct initial review of documents and plans. If complete: schedule inspection. If incomplete: return documents to client with explanation.; Fee: None; Processing time: 10 minutes; Person responsible: Administrative Aide IV 2. Agency action: Conduct actual inspection of the area/structure and its status, and prepare a report; Fee: None; Processing time: 1 day; Person responsible: Housing & Homesite Regulations Officer IV, Administrative Aide IV 3. Agency action: Conduct evaluation and finalize documents and plans; Fee: None; Processing time: 2 hours; Person responsible: Engineer II 4. Agency action: Prepare recommendation based on the results of evaluation and inspection; Fee: None; Processing time: 2 hours; Person responsible: Housing & Homesite Regulation Officer V 5. Client step: Find out result of inspection and evaluation; Agency action: If approved: issue Order of Payment. If disapproved: return documents to client with explanation.; Fee: None; Processing time: 10 minutes; Person responsible: Administrative Aide IV 6. Client step: Pay the corresponding amount; Agency action: Accept payment and issue official receipt; Fee: Based on National Building Code Fees + Php30.00 for documentary stamp; Processing time: 2 minutes; Person responsible: Revenue Collection Clerk III (Treasury Office) 7. Client step: Receive the Building Permit; Agency action: Process the Building Permit; Fee: None; Processing time: 5 minutes; Person responsible: Administrative Aide IV 8. Agency action: Approve and sign the Building Permit; Fee: None; Processing time: 2 minutes; Person responsible: Department Head 9. Agency action: Release the Building Permit and record receipt by the applicant; Fee: None; Processing time: 10 minutes; Person responsible: Administrative Aide IV

chunks.office: City Social Services Department - Special Social Services Division
chunks.text: Mediation Dialogue / Family Conference Assistance Process Flow (step-by-step): 1. Client step: Go to the City Social Services Department and report the concern; Agency action: Conduct the initial Intake interview using the WCPU intake Sheet.; Fee: None; Processing time: 20 minutes; Person responsible: Social Worker, Support Staff 2. Agency action: Assess the concern.; Fee: None; Processing time: 5 minutes 3. Client step: Give preferred schedule for the dialogue; Agency action: Prepare and issue the Letter of Invitation.; Fee: None; Processing time: 5 minutes; Person responsible: Support Staff 4. Client step: Send the Letter of Invitation to the other party; Fee: None 5. Client step: Go to the City Social Services Department on the scheduled date for the dialogue; Agency action: Conduct the dialogue between both parties.; Fee: None; Processing time: 2 hours; Person responsible: Social Worker 6. Client step: Sign the agreement; Agency action: Prepare the agreement, re-explain the outcome of the dialogue, and have both parties sign.; Fee: None; Processing time: 20 minutes; Person responsible: Social Worker 7. Agency action: Monitor and evaluate compliance of both parties with the agreement.; Fee: None; Person responsible: Support Staff 8. Agency action: Call both parties after a month and conduct a home visit after three months.; Fee: None 9. Agency action: Prepare the Progress Report.; Fee: None; Processing time: 2 hours 10. Client step: If no agreement was reached and one party wishes to file a case: wait for the referral letter from the Social Worker; Agency action: Prepare and issue the Referral Letter to be brought to the Public Attorney's Office.; Fee: None; Processing time: 5 minutes; Person responsible: Social Worker 11. If needed, refer to a Psychologist for Psychological Assessment.; Fee: None; Processing time: No fixed duration; Person responsible: Social Worker 5. Client step: Go to the PNP and Office of the Clerk of Court with the Social Worker; Agency action: Provide the appropriate intervention based on the victim's needs: if not filing a case, assist in obtaining a Protection Order for the victim; if filing a case, accompany to PNP for a sworn statement and to the Office of the Clerk of Court to file the case; if protective custody is needed, process the required documents for a residential care facility; if returning to family, conduct Reintegration and coordinate with the C/MSWDO of their area, requesting a PCAR for possible reunification, and refer to financial assistance if the family cannot cover travel expenses.; Fee: None; Processing time: No fixed duration; 1 day for reintegration coordination steps; Person responsible: Social Worker 6. chunks.text: Handling of Foundling, Abandoned, and Voluntarily/Involuntarily Committed Children Process Flow (step-by-step): 1. Client step: Go to the City Social Services Office and report the concern; Fee: None 2. Client step: Submit the Intake Sheet from the barangay or PNP; Agency action: Accept and review the document, and log in the logbook.; Fee: None; Processing time: 5 minutes; Person responsible: Social Worker, Support Staff 3. Agency action: Conduct the initial Intake Interview using the WCPU Intake Sheet.; Fee: None; Processing time: 20 minutes 4. Agency action: Report to the Barangay or PNP for the Blotter Report.; Fee: None; Processing time: 10 minutes; Person responsible: Social Worker 5. Agency action: Process the requirements needed to temporarily place the child in a residential care facility. If the child is voluntarily committed/surrendered/neglected/abandoned, first request a Deed of Voluntary Commitment (DVC).; Fee: None; Processing time: 30 minutes; Person responsible: Social Worker 6. Agency action: Process the documents needed to immediately transfer the child to a Child-Caring/Child-Placing Agency (CCA/CPA).; Fee: None; Processing time: 1 day 7. Agency action: Continue coordination with the CCA/CPA to complete all required documents.; Fee: None; Processing time: No fixed duration

chunks.title: Conducting an Emergency Reach-Out Operation
chunks.office: City Social Services Department - Special Social Services Division
chunks.text: Conducting an Emergency Reach-Out Operation Process Flow (step-by-step): 1. Client step: Call or go to the City Social Services Office to request an Emergency Rescue; Agency action: Answer the call or receive the request.; Fee: None; Processing time: 10 minutes; Person responsible: Social Worker 2. Agency action: Accept and review the documents.; Fee: None; Processing time: 45 minutes 3. Agency action: Conduct the Risk and Safety Assessment. If the child's/victim's life is not in danger per the assessment: provide the appropriate intervention based on need. If the assessment finds a reach-out operation is needed: conduct the reach-out operation.; Fee: None; Processing time: No fixed duration; Person responsible: Social Worker, PNP 4. Agency action: Conduct the initial Intake Interview with the rescued child/victim.; Fee: None; Processing time: 20 minutes; Person responsible: Social Worker 5. Agency action: If the child/victim requires a Medico-Legal/Physical Examination: refer to PNP. If not required: process the documents needed to bring the child/victim to a residential care facility and provide protective custody, including preparing an After Reach-Out Operation Report and Social Case Study Report.; Fee: None; Processing time: 1 hour; Person responsible: Social Worker 6. Agency action: Accompany the victim to the PNP for the process of filing a case.; Fee: None; Person responsible: Social Worker

Certificate of Live Birth (secure from: PSA) - Marriage Certificate, or Divorce/Declaration of Nullity of Marriage/Legal Separation documents (secure from: PSA) - Medical Certificate issued within 6 months from time of application (secure from: Licensed Physician) - Latest Income Tax Return or Certificate of Employment or other proof of income (secure from: Bureau of Internal Revenue) - Original copy of NBI/Police Clearance issued within a year from date of application (secure from: NBI / PNP) - Original copy of Barangay Certificate stating residency, length of residence, and good moral character (secure from: Barangay Hall) - Whole Body Picture taken within 6 months of application, with date indicated (secure from: Applicant) - Photograph of interior and exterior of the applicant's house (secure from: Applicant) - Philhealth ID (photocopy) and updated Members Data Record or HMO record (if HMO allows declaring a foster child as dependent) (secure from: Applicant) - Written consent of biological children aged 10 and above living in the household (secure from: Biological Children) - Signed Undertaking on Child Protection Code and Code of Conduct of Foster Parents (secure from: Regional Alternative Child Care Office (RACCO)) - Certificate of Attendance at Foster Care Forum (digital copy accepted) (secure from: RACCO) - Original copy of letters from 3 non-relative Character References who have known the applicant for at least 3 years (secure from: Applicant) - Such other documents that the NACC, CPA, or LGU may require (secure from: )

chunks.title: Foster Care Application
chunks.office: City Social Services Department - Special Social Services Division
chunks.text: Foster Care Application Process Flow (step-by-step): 1. Client step: Attend the Online Forum (client/petitioner); Agency action: Provide the RACCO Online Forum link.; Fee: None; Processing time: 3 hours; Person responsible: Social Worker 2. Client step: Fill out the Undertaking and Application Form; Fee: None 3. Client step: Have the required documents reviewed before submitting to RACCO; Agency action: Review the documents and assist the client/petitioner in completing them.; Fee: None; Processing time: 5 minutes; Person responsible: Social Worker 4. Agency action: Conduct home visitation and interview once the letter from RACCO is received, to gather information needed for the Home Study Report.; Fee: None; Processing time: Within 5 days; Person responsible: Social Worker 5. Agency action: Prepare the Foster Care Home Study Report and submit to RACCO.; Fee: None; Processing time: 20 days 6. Agency action: Go to the RACCO Office and submit the Foster Care Application.; Fee: None; Processing time: 1 day 7. Agency action: Wait for RACCO's decision and request copies of submitted documents plus the recommendation letter.; Fee: None; Processing time: No fixed duration; Person responsible: RACCO 8. Client step: Wait for the application result (may file a Motion for Reconsideration); Agency action: If approved: RACCO issues the Foster Care License and Identification Card. If not approved: assist the petitioner in completing requirements per RACCO's recommendation.; Fee: None; Processing time: No fixed duration; Person responsible: RACCO, Social Worker

Client step: Go to RACCO's Office and submit the application; Agency action: Accompany the petitioner to RACCO's Office.; Fee: None; Processing time: Per RACCO's schedule; Person responsible: Social Worker 8. Client step: Wait for the letter with the decision on the application; request copies of submitted documents with the letter from RACCO; Fee: None; Person responsible: Social Worker

chunks.text: Application for Leave (Without Commutation of Leave Credits) (Aplikasyon sa pagliban sa trabaho) Office or Division: CHRMO – Personnel Transaction Division Classification: Simple Type of Transaction: G2G – Government to Government (internal) Who may avail: Empleyado ng Pamahalaang Lungsod Checklist of Requirements: - Leave Application Form (LAF) (CS Form No. 6 Revised 2020) (2 kopya) (secure from: CSC Website o Administrative Officer ng Tanggapan) - Clearance from Money, Property and Work-related Accountabilities (if more than 30 days leave) (secure from: Kliyente) - Kung Sick Leave na hihigit sa 5 araw: Medical Certificate o Affidavit (secure from: Doktor / Abogado) - Kung Maternity Leave: Katunayan ng pagbubuntis (secure from: Doktor o Ospital) - Kung Paternity Leave: Katunayan ng Panganganak; Accomplished Notice of Allocation of Maternity Leave Credits (CS Form No. 6a) (secure from: City Civil Registry Office o Ospital / CSC Website) - Kung Solo Parent Leave: Valid Solo Parent Identification Card (secure from: City Social Services Department) - Kung Study Leave: Kontrata sa pagitan ng empleyado at ng Pamahalaang Lungsod (secure from: Kliyente) - Kung VAWC Leave: BPO / TPO-PPO / Sertipikasyon / Police Report at medical certificate (secure from: Barangay / Korte / Tanggapan ng Pulisya at Doktor) - Kung Rehabilitation Leave: Sulat Kahilingan; Medical Certificate; Kasulatan ng pagsang-ayon ng government physician (secure from: Kliyente / Lisensyadong Doktor o Ospital) - Kung Special Privilege Leave Benefits for Women: Medical Certificate kalakip ng clinical summary (secure from: Lisensyadong Doktor o Ospital) - Kung Adoption Leave: Pre-adoptive Placement Authority (1 authenticated copy) (secure from: DSWD)

chunks.title: Application for Leave (Without Commutation of Leave Credits)
chunks.office: CHRMO – Personnel Transaction Division
chunks.text: Application for Leave (Without Commutation of Leave Credits) Process Flow (step-by-step): 1. Client step: 1. Punan ang lahat ng mga kinakailangan sa pormularyo, at isumite ito at ang mga iba pang kailangang dokumento; Agency action: 1.1 Tanggapin at suriin ang isinumiteng pormularyo at mga kinakailangan; 1.2 Itala ang aplikasyon sa itinalagang monitoring sheet at ibigay sa magpoproseso; 1.3 Itala ang aplikasyon sa system, tuusin ang leave balances at itala sa leave card; 1.4 Suriin ang aplikasyon at leave card at patunayan ang leave balances; 1.5 Ipadala sa CAO o OCM para sa huling aksyon; 1.6 Aksyunan ang aplikasyon; 1.7 Ipadala sa CHRMO muli ang aplikasyong may aksyon; 1.8 Itala ang aplikasyon at desisyon sa system; 1.9 Ipadala sa empleyado ang isang kopya; Fee: Walang Babayaran; Processing time: 1 araw*; Person responsible: Contract of Service; City Human Resource Mngt. Officer; City Administrator or City Mayor 2. Client step: 2. Pirmahan ang log sheet at tanggapin ang aplikasyong may aksyon; Agency action: 2. Ipatanggap ang aplikasyong may aksyon sa empleyado; Processing time: 10 minuto; Person responsible: Contract of Service

chunks.title: Application for Leave (With Commutation of Leave Credits)

chunks.title: Application for Leave (With Commutation of Leave Credits)
chunks.office: CHRMO – Personnel Transaction Division
chunks.text: Application for Leave (With Commutation of Leave Credits) Process Flow (step-by-step): 1. Client step: 1. Punan ang lahat ng mga kinakailangan sa pormularyo, at isumite ito at ang mga iba pang kailangang dokumento; Agency action: 1.1–1.9 Kagyat na pagpoproseso, pagtala sa system, pagpapadala sa CAO/OCM, aksyon, at pagbabalik sa CHRMO at sa empleyado; Fee: Walang Babayaran; Processing time: 1 araw*; Person responsible: Contract of Service; City Human Resource Mngt. Officer; City Administrator or City Mayor 2. Client step: 2. Pirmahan ang log sheet at tanggapin ang aplikasyong may aksyon; Agency action: 2.1 Ipatanggap ang aplikasyong may aksyon; 2.2 Kung Terminal Leave, ihanda ang Service Record at Summary of Leave Balances; 2.3 Ipatanggap sa City Accounting & Internal Control Office ang aplikasyon; 2.4 Gawan ng voucher para sa pagbabayad; 2.5 Ipatanggap sa City Budget Management Office; 2.6 Siyasatin kung may sapat na pondo at pirmahan ang voucher; 2.7 Ibalik sa CAICO at itala sa system; 2.8 Pirmahan ang voucher; 2.9 Dalhin sa CTMO upang mabayaran; Processing time: 2 araw 5 oras 12 minuto; Person responsible: Administrative Officer IV; City Accounting & Internal Control Office; City Budget Management Office; City Accountant 3. Client step: 3. Tanggapin ang sahod sa ATM o sa CTMO kung Over the Counter (OTC); Agency action: 3.1 Bayaran ang benepisyo sa angkop na pamamaraan; Processing time: 4 oras; Person responsible: City Treasury Management Office

chunks.title: Cooperatives And Livelihood Development Department - Contact Information
chunks.text: Cooperatives And Livelihood Development Department - Contact Information Department Head: Mr. Leonardo F. Opulencia Sr. Location: Right Wing, Lower Ground Floor, New City Hall of Calamba Phone: (049) 545-6789 loc 8018/8019 Email: cccldd@yahoo.com About this office: The City of Calamba Cooperatives and Livelihood Development Department promotes a culture of entrepreneurship among Calambeños and strengthens the cooperative movement in the city, facilitating cooperative organization and development through markets, training, facilities, technology and funds.

chunks.title: Housing And Settlements Department - Contact Information
chunks.text: Housing And Settlements Department - Contact Information Department Head: Mr. Ronaldo M. Dela Cruz Location: Left Wing, Lower Ground Floor, New City Hall of Calamba Phone: (049) 545-6789 loc 8020/8021 About this office: Provide technical and staff services to the Local Chief Executive and other local officials in the formulation and implementation of housing and settlements programs in the City of Calamba.

chunks.title: Information, Investment Promotions And Employment Services Office - Contact Information
chunks.text: Information, Investment Promotions And Employment Services Office - Contact Information Department Head: Ms. Noemi E. Talatala Location: Lower Ground Floor, Left Wing, New City Hall of Calamba Phone: (049) 545-6789 local 8011/8012/8014 Email: iipeso@calambacity.gov.ph Facebook: iipeso calamba About this office: To provide relevant, adequate and timely information to the City and its residents, and furnish information and data affecting the development and programs of its local government. This office is in charge of employment facilitation programs and investment promotions.

chunks.title: Sangguniang Panlungsod - Legislative Services Office - Contact Information
chunks.text: Sangguniang Panlungsod - Legislative Services Office - Contact Information Department Head: Atty. Noel M. Villanueva Location: Right Wing, 3rd Floor, New City Hall of Calamba Phone: (049) 545-6789 loc. 8312/8314 About this office: To provide legislative support to the Sangguniang Panlungsod as stated in Section 469 of the Local Government Code of 1991.

chunks.title: Public Order And Safety Office - Contact Information
chunks.text: Public Order And Safety Office - Contact Information Department Head: Mr. Edwin A. Nuñez Location: 2nd Floor, CDRRM Bldg., New City Hall Compound Phone: (049) 545-6789 loc 8024/8025/8026 Email: poso@calambacity.gov.ph About this office: For the purpose of providing effective traffic and transportation management, enforcing national laws and local ordinances (including City Ordinance No. 511, S. 2011, the 2011 Calamba City Traffic Code) to promote a disciplined society and safe environment.

chunks.title: Veterinary Services And Slaughterhouse Management Office - Contact Information
chunks.text: Veterinary Services And Slaughterhouse Management Office - Contact Information Department Head: Dr. Sheila A. Matibag Location: Right Wing, Lower Ground Flr., New City Hall of Calamba Phone: (049) 545-6789 loc 8003/8004 Facebook: City Veterinary Office of Calamba About this office: For an effective delivery of the basic services being offered by the City Veterinary and Slaughterhouse Management Department to clients from the City of Calamba, through research, training, and public seminars promoting self-reliance.

chunks.title: City College Of Calamba - Contact Information
chunks.text: City College Of Calamba - Contact Information Department Head: Dr. Ronald A. Gonzales Location: Old Municipal Site, Brgy. VII, Poblacion, Calamba City Phone: (049) 545-0160/545-0555/502-0677 About this office: The City College of Calamba serves as the city's local higher education institution, providing accessible tertiary education to Calambeño residents.

chunks.title: City Administration Office - Contact Information
chunks.text: City Administration Office - Contact Information Department Head: Mr. Johnny R. Pamuspusan Location: Right Wing, 3rd Floor, New City Hall of Calamba Phone: (049) 545-6789 loc 8300/8301/8302/8303 About this office: Exercise general supervision and control over all programs, projects, services and activities of the City Government; formulate measures for the Sangguniang Panlungsod; provide support to the Mayor; establish and maintain a sound personnel program for the Local Government Unit.

chunks.title: Business Permits And Tricycle Franchising Office - Contact Information
chunks.text: Business Permits And Tricycle Franchising Office - Contact Information Department Head: Ms. Bernadette D. Opulencia Location: Right Wing, Ground Floor, New City Hall of Calamba Phone: (049) 545-6789 - Business Permits: loc 8101 - Working Permits: loc 8104 - Tricycle Franchising: loc 8102 Email: lgucalambabptfo@gmail.com About this office: Responsible for the processing and issuance of Business and Working Permits and Tricycle Franchises, monitoring and inspection of all business establishments and tricycle units operating within the city, and for the assessment and imposition of proper business taxes and regulatory fees.

chunks.title: City Accounting & Internal Control Office - Contact Information
chunks.text: City Accounting & Internal Control Office - Contact Information Department Head: Ms. Editha M. Malabanan Location: Left Wing, 2nd Floor, New City of Calamba Phone: (049) 545-6789 loc 8203/8204 About this office: To take charge of the accounting and internal audit services of the local government unit.

chunks.title: Buildings Regulatory Services Department - Contact Information
chunks.text: Buildings Regulatory Services Department - Contact Information Department Head: Engr. Joselito Guevarra Location: Right Wing, 2nd Floor, New City Hall of Calamba Phone: (049) 545-6789 loc 8030/8031 About this office: Created pursuant to P.D. 1096, otherwise known as the National Building Code of the Philippines, and has primary jurisdiction on matters relevant to and defined under P.D. 1096.

chunks.title: City Agricultural Services Office - Contact Information
chunks.text: City Agricultural Services Office - Contact Information Department Head: Ms. Ruby V. Arenas Location: Right Wing, Lower Ground Floor, New City Hall of Calamba Phone: (049) 545-6789 loc 8001/8002 About this office: The Department is mandated to develop/implement plans and programs relative to agriculture and aquaculture that will ensure maximum assistance to farmers, including subsidized inputs, technology transfer, and technical assistance.

chunks.title: City Assessment Office - Contact Information
chunks.text: City Assessment Office - Contact Information Department Head: Mr. Graciano G. Aldabe Location: Right Wing, Ground Floor, New City Hall of Calamba Phone: (049) 545-6789 loc. 8107/8108/8109 About this office: To generate local revenues through real property tax by means of new assessment and re-assessment within the jurisdiction of Calamba City, rendering prompt, efficient, friendly and courteous public service.
